ideas.title: A Station for Every Place
ideas.pitch: Tie a station to a zone, a kind of duty or your home, so the radio changes with where you are and goes back when you leave.
ideas.experience: You set your chill station for your house and a loud one for high-end duties. The queue pops, you zone into the savage fight, and the heavy station starts on the loading screen. When the duty ends and you are back in Limsa, your usual station picks up again.
ideas.how: Configuration gains a list of rules (territory id, or a content type from the ContentFinderCondition sheet, or 'housing') to a station Id, like LastStationId. Plugin subscribes to IClientState.TerritoryChanged and IDutyState.DutyStarted, finds the first matching rule, and calls Radio.PlayStationAsync through Plugin.Run with the matching entry of Radio.Stations. The station before the rule is remembered and restored when no rule matches. MainWindow gets a 'Stations for places' section with a 'this zone' button that fills in IClientState.TerritoryType. Zone names come from the TerritoryType sheet through IDataManager.
ideas.risks: Switching stations throws away the current song and fetches a fresh playlist, so rapid zoning (a housing ward tour) would burn through songs; switches need a short settle time. A rule pointing at a station you deleted must fail quietly. Pandora limits how many songs you may skip an hour on some accounts, and changing station is not a skip, but it should be checked.
ideas.audience: players who keep the radio on all evening

ideas.title: Let the Boss Theme Play
ideas.pitch: Pick duties where the game's own music matters, and XivPiano steps aside there: the radio pauses and the game's music comes back.
ideas.experience: You love the radio for levelling, but not over a trial's theme. You tick 'the game's music in trials and raids'. The instance loads, the song fades out, the boss theme swells, and when you leave the duty your station carries on from where it paused.
ideas.how: In Plugin.OnUpdate, beside the cutscene pause, a 'step aside' check: ICondition BoundByDuty plus the duty's ContentType (from IDutyState and the ContentFinderCondition sheet) against a set in Configuration. It pauses with Radio.TogglePause like pausedForCutscene does, with its own flag. The music muting needs no change: OnUpdate already puts IsSndBgm back as it was whenever the radio stops playing.
ideas.risks: A paused song's audio link can expire during a long raid, so resuming may skip to a fresh song; Radio already does that quietly. Two reasons to pause (a cutscene inside a duty) must not resume each other too early, so the flags need to be kept apart and tested.
ideas.audience: everyone who has a favourite boss theme

ideas.title: Quieter While Someone Speaks
ideas.pitch: Lower the radio while a dialogue box is open, and bring it back up when the talking is over, instead of only pausing for full cutscenes.
ideas.experience: An NPC stops you in the street with a voiced line. The song dips to a murmur so you can hear her, and rises back to its volume a moment after you close the box.
ideas.how: An IAddonLifecycle listener on the Talk addon (PostSetup and PreFinalize) sets a 'ducked' flag in Plugin. AudioOut.Volume is ramped over about 300 ms toward Config.Volume times a duck factor (Configuration.DuckTo, default 25%) from Plugin.OnUpdate, and back when the flag clears. AudioOut already applies Volume per sample in MpegSampleProvider.Read, so the ramp is a few lines.
ideas.risks: The plugin cannot tell a voiced line from a silent one, so it ducks for every dialogue box; that has to be a setting. The ramp must never fight the volume slider in MainWindow. Talk is not the only dialogue addon (battle talk, some quest windows), so the first version will miss some.
ideas.audience: story players, anyone doing MSQ with the radio on

ideas.title: Crossfade Between Songs
ideas.pitch: Fade the end of one song into the start of the next, so the radio flows like a mix instead of stopping and starting.
ideas.experience: The last chorus of a song fades under the first bars of the next. There is no gap of silence while the next song downloads, even on a slow evening connection.
ideas.how: AudioOut today holds one WaveOutEvent and one MpegSampleProvider. It would build one output over a MixingSampleProvider fed by two MpegSampleProviders, with a PrepareAsync(Track) that downloads the next song while the current one plays (Radio.AdvanceAsync already keeps one song in hand in its queue). A fade of a few seconds starts when Position reaches Duration minus the fade length, and the Ended event moves to the fade start so Radio advances then. Crossfade length and 'off' go in Configuration.
ideas.risks: Two songs in memory at once, a few MB each, which is fine. Thumbs and 'why this song?' act on Radio.Current, so the switch-over moment must be clear or a thumb could land on the wrong song. Replay gain differs per song; each keeps its own gain factor. Songs with long silent endings make the fade point a guess.
ideas.audience: everyone, especially on long play sessions

ideas.title: Share What's Playing
ideas.pitch: One button copies a line about the song, with its Pandora link, ready to paste into party, FC or linkshell chat.
ideas.experience: Your static asks what this song is on voice. You press Share, type /fc, paste, and your FC reads '♪ Title by Artist, on Pandora' with the link, while the song carries on.
ideas.how: A Share button in MainWindow.DrawControls builds the line from Radio.Current (Title, Artist, Album and DetailUrl, Pandora's page for the song, which Track already carries) and puts it on the clipboard with ImGui.SetClipboardText. A matching '/piano share' copies it too. Nothing is sent by the plugin: the player pastes it into whichever channel they choose.
ideas.risks: Automatically posting to party or FC chat would be a plugin sending chat for you, which Square Enix's terms and Dalamud's rules frown on, so this only fills the clipboard. Some players will find the extra paste a nuisance, and that is the price. DetailUrl can be empty; the line must read well without it.
ideas.audience: FCs, statics, friends who swap music

ideas.title: Now Playing on Your Lantern
ideas.pitch: With XivLantern installed, your friends can see what you are listening to next to your lit lantern, if you say so.
ideas.experience: You open XivLantern and your friend's line reads 'Listening to Clair de Lune on Classical Piano'. You like it, so you start the same kind of station yourself.
ideas.how: XivPiano already offers XivPiano.NowPlaying over IPC. XivLantern would gain an opt-in to read it and add 'listening to' to the presence note it already shares with friends; nothing in XivPiano changes except a new XivPiano.SongChanged message gate (see piano-song-events) so XivLantern does not have to poll. Off by default in both plugins.
ideas.risks: It needs work in XivLantern, which only has XivLantern.v1.GetStatus today, and XivLantern's promise is that nothing from the game is sent; a song title is not from the game, but it is still something about you going to others, so it must be plainly opt-in. Song titles can be long and need cutting.

ideas.title: Listen Together
ideas.pitch: A party or linkshell tunes in to the same station's seeds together, each person on their own Pandora account, with play and pause kept in step.
ideas.experience: Your FC's Friday night: the host starts 'Listen together' on a synthwave station and shares a short code. Each friend pastes it and a station built from the same artists starts for them. When the host pauses for a mechanic explanation, everyone's radio pauses too.
ideas.how: The code carries the station's seeds (from station.getStation with includeExtendedAttributes, as pianobar asks for them) as music tokens. Each listener's XivPiano makes a station with station.createStation from the first and adds the rest with station.addMusic, then plays it. Play and pause travel as small messages over XivLantern's channels when it is installed, or not at all. Nothing but the code and play/pause state is shared.
ideas.risks: Every listener hears different songs, because Pandora makes a playlist per listener and XivPiano will never pass audio from one player to another (that would be rebroadcasting, which Pandora's terms forbid). So 'together' means the same kind of music, not the same song, and the page must say that honestly. Everyone needs a US Pandora account. It adds a station to each listener's list, which they may not want to keep.

ideas.title: Add Variety to a Station
ideas.pitch: See what a station is built from, add an artist or song to it, and take back a thumb you regret, without leaving the game.
ideas.experience: Your 'Final Fantasy Soundtracks' station has gone stale. You open its seeds, search for a composer and add them. The next few songs bring in pieces you have not heard, and you remove a thumbs-down you gave by mistake last week.
ideas.how: PandoraClient gains GetStationAsync (station.getStation with includeExtendedAttributes, returning seeds and feedback), AddMusicAsync (station.addMusic with a musicToken from SearchAsync), DeleteMusicAsync (station.deleteMusic with the seedId) and DeleteFeedbackAsync (station.deleteFeedback with the feedbackId), the calls pianobar makes in src/libpiano/request.c. MainWindow gets a 'Station details' popup reusing the search box from DrawNewStation. Host tests go into PandoraTests against the fake Pandora.
ideas.risks: More Pandora calls means more of an unofficial API to keep working. A station must keep at least one seed, and Pandora's answer to removing the last must read clearly. Shared stations cannot be edited until they are made your own (piano-adopt-shared).

ideas.title: Browse Pandora's Genre Stations
ideas.pitch: A list of Pandora's own genre stations by category, to start one with a click when you do not know what you want.
ideas.experience: You open 'Genres', pick Ambient, then 'Video Game Music', and a station starts playing without you having to think of an artist.
ideas.how: PandoraClient.GetGenreStationsAsync calls station.getGenreStations and returns categories of (name, stationToken). A 'Genres' tab in MainWindow lists them; picking one runs Radio.CreateAndPlayAsync with PandoraClient.CreateStationAsync on that genre station's token, the way pianobar makes a station from a genre. The list is cached for the session.
ideas.risks: Pandora has changed its genre catalogue over the years and this call may return fewer genres than the web app shows. Each pick adds a station to the list, and Pandora caps how many stations you may have (PandoraException.StationLimit already explains it).
ideas.audience: new Pandora users, anyone out of ideas

ideas.title: Choose What Shuffle Mixes
ideas.pitch: Tick which stations Shuffle draws from, the way Pandora's QuickMix lets you.
ideas.experience: Your Shuffle keeps playing a kids' station someone set up years ago. You untick it in XivPiano's list and Shuffle plays only your own music from then on.
ideas.how: Station already knows IsQuickMix. PandoraClient.GetStationsAsync would also read quickMixStationIds from the QuickMix station in the user.getStationList answer, and a new SetQuickMixAsync sends user.setQuickMix with the chosen quickMixStationIds, as pianobar does. MainWindow.DrawStations shows a checkbox per station when 'Edit Shuffle' is on.
ideas.risks: Changes apply to the account everywhere, including the Pandora app, which is the point but should be said. The field is not present for every account type, so the checkboxes must hide when it is missing.

ideas.title: Station Modes
ideas.pitch: Pick a station's mode (My Station, Crowd Faves, Deep Cuts, Discovery, Newly Released, Artist Only) where Pandora offers them to your account.
ideas.experience: Your favourite band's station has played the same five hits all week. You switch it to Deep Cuts and the next songs are album tracks you had forgotten about.
ideas.how: pianobar asks for modes with interactiveradio.v1.getAvailableModesSimple (stationId) and sets one with interactiveradio.v1.setAndGetAvailableModes (stationId, modeId), through the same JSON API and Blowfish wrapping PandoraClient.CallAsync already does. A mode picker beside the station name in MainWindow.DrawNowPlaying; a mode change clears Radio's queue so the next song follows it.
ideas.risks: These calls are newer than the rest and less documented; whether they answer for the Android and Pandora One partners XivPiano signs in as, and for free accounts, has to be found out first. Pandora offers different modes per station, so the picker must list only what the answer says.
ideas.audience: Plus and Premium listeners, long-time Pandora users

ideas.title: Explicit Content Filter
ideas.pitch: Turn Pandora's explicit content filter on or off from XivPiano's settings, for streaming or a shared room.
ideas.experience: You stream your gameplay on Saturday. You tick 'Filter explicit songs' in XivPiano and Pandora stops sending explicit tracks until you untick it.
ideas.how: PandoraClient gains GetSettingsAsync (user.getSettings, reading isExplicitContentFilterEnabled) and ChangeSettingsAsync (user.changeSettings with isExplicitContentFilterEnabled), as pianobar's settings menu does; changeSettings wants the current username and password, which PandoraClient keeps for the session in its credentials field. A checkbox in MainWindow.DrawSettings, read after sign-in. Queued songs are dropped after a change so the filter applies from the next song.
ideas.risks: It is an account setting, so it changes the Pandora app and website too. If the password was not kept, a change needs it typed again. Songs already fetched still play until the queue is refilled.

ideas.title: Make a Shared Station Your Own
ideas.pitch: Turn a station someone shared with you into your own copy, so your thumbs teach it and you can edit its seeds.
ideas.experience: A friend shared their 'Gridanian Folk' station and you added it on Pandora's site. In XivPiano it is marked as shared; you press 'Make it mine' and from then on your thumbs up count.
ideas.how: Station already carries IsShared from user.getStationList. PandoraClient.TransformSharedStationAsync calls station.transformSharedStation with the stationToken, as pianobar does, and Radio replaces the station in Radio.Stations with the answer. MainWindow shows a small 'shared' tag and the button.
ideas.risks: Few people use shared stations any more, so it is small value. The transformed station gets a new token, so LastStationId and any piano-duty-stations rules pointing at the old one need updating.
ideas.audience: players who swap stations with friends

ideas.title: What Was That Song?
ideas.pitch: A list of the last twenty songs, with thumbs, bookmark and 'why this song?' still working on them after they have finished.
ideas.experience: A song played during a pull and you were too busy to look. After the wipe you open History, find it second from the top, thumb it up and bookmark it.
ideas.how: Radio already keeps the last Radio.HistoryLength (20) finished tracks in Radio.History. A History tab in MainWindow lists them with the same icon buttons as DrawControls; thumbs call PandoraClient.AddFeedbackAsync with the old track's StationId and Token (pianobar rates songs from its history the same way), and bookmarks and ExplainAsync take the Token as they do now. Album art reuses LoadArtAsync.
ideas.risks: A thumb on an old song must go to the station it played on, which may not be the current one; Track.StationId has it, but the station token must be looked up. Pandora may refuse feedback on a very old track token, and the error has to read plainly. History is lost when the game closes unless it is saved.

ideas.title: Other Plugins Hear the Song Change
ideas.pitch: Tell other plugins the moment the song changes, so XivMcp, Ghostty or a Stream Deck setup can react without asking every second.
ideas.experience: You ask Almanac through XivMcp 'what was that song?' and it answers from the event it heard. Your Stream Deck's 'next' button runs a macro with /piano next and its label updates with the new title.
ideas.how: A message gate XivPiano.SongChanged next to the existing XivPiano.NowPlaying and XivPiano.Control, sent with ICallGateProvider.SendMessage from Plugin.OnUpdate where announcedToken already notices a new track, carrying the same JSON NowPlayingJson builds. XivMcp could add read and control tools that call NowPlaying and Control. Stream Deck works today through macros with /piano; the event is for plugins that show state.
ideas.risks: Subscribers run on the framework thread, so a slow one would stall the game; the docs must say to return quickly. The JSON shape becomes a contract to keep. XivMcp's control tools would need the same in-game approval as its other actions.
ideas.audience: plugin authors, XivMcp and Stream Deck users

ideas.title: Scrobble to Last.fm
ideas.pitch: Send what you listen to in game to your Last.fm profile, as Elpis does, if you sign in to Last.fm.
ideas.experience: Your Last.fm profile has years of listening, and the hours in Eorzea were missing from it. You connect it once in XivPiano's settings and your raid night's songs show up under your recent tracks.
ideas.how: A small Last.fm client in XivPiano.Core (Elpis has one in Libs/LastFmScrobbler): desktop auth once, then track.updateNowPlaying when Radio.Current changes and track.scrobble when a song has played for half its length or four minutes, measured from AudioOut.Position, queued and retried while offline. The session key is kept with Secrets (DPAPI) like the Pandora password. Needs a Last.fm API key registered for XivPiano.
ideas.risks: A second network destination, which the privacy note must name, and off by default. Last.fm's own terms apply to the API key. Skipped and banned songs must not scrobble. Scrobble rules about minimum length (30 seconds) must be kept.

ideas.title: Media Keys and Hotkeys
ideas.pitch: Play, pause and skip with your keyboard's media keys, or a key of your choosing, while the game has focus.
ideas.experience: Mid-dungeon, a song you do not like starts. You press the next-track key on your keyboard and it skips, without opening a window or typing a command.
ideas.how: Dalamud's IKeyState reads keys while the game window has focus; Plugin.OnUpdate would watch the media keys (VK_MEDIA_PLAY_PAUSE, VK_MEDIA_NEXT_TRACK) and any keys set in Configuration, and call Plugin.Control('toggle') or Control('next') on a fresh press. Elpis does the same outside a game with global hotkeys (Elpis/Hotkeys.cs); here only in-focus keys are planned.
ideas.risks: Whether Wine passes media keys to the game at all has to be found out, and the desktop's own media player may take them first. A bound key must not also trigger a game action, and IKeyState cannot stop the game seeing it, so plain keys are risky and chords are safer. Macros with /piano already cover most of this.

ideas.title: Lyrics, Where Licensed
ideas.pitch: Show the words of the song that is playing, if a licensed source that allows it can be found.
ideas.experience: A song you half know comes on. You open the Lyrics tab and read along while you craft.
ideas.how: Pandora's partner API that pianobar documents has no lyrics call, and Pandora's own apps show lyrics from a licensed provider through their private web API, which XivPiano does not use. So this would mean a lyrics provider whose terms allow a third-party player to show them, keyed on Track.Title and Track.Artist, shown in a tab in MainWindow.
ideas.risks: Lyrics are licensed separately from the music. Scraping them from lyrics sites, or lifting Pandora's own, would break someone's terms and their licence, which is why this is marked unsafe as it stands. It is listed to see whether people want it enough to look for a proper licence; without one it will not be built.
